leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, Section 15(1)
leads.documents: Constitutional equality guarantee that underpins LGBTQ legal status in Manitoba; text quoted in article and interpreted to cover sexual orientation, transsexuality and HIV status as analogous grounds.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: s.15(1) text quoted; Constitution included 1982, came into force 1985; reaffirmed 2008 equality language.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada (1995) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is constitutionally protected under s.15 equality clause as an analogous ground; basis for equal protection claims in Manitoba.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'landmark decision in 1995, Egan v Canada' and 'Egan v. Canada' discussion of s.15.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta (1998) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Held failure of a provincial legislature to include sexual orientation in human rights law violates s.15; led to all provinces, territories and federal government explicitly including sexual orientation and gender identity by 2017, including Manitoba.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: '1998 decision in Vriend v Alberta'.

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (federal, 2005)
leads.documents: Legalized same-sex marriage nationwide, first in Americas; applies in Manitoba and confirms federal jurisdiction over capacity to marry.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'Parliament passed the bill on July 20, 2005' after Supreme Court reference December 2004 declaring proposed definition consistent with Charter.

leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Decriminalized same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults; brought into force upon royal assent June 27, 1969; foundational criminal-law status applicable in Manitoba.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (also known as Bill C-150)' brought into force June 27, 1969.

leads.title: Criminal Code s.159 repeal via Bill C-32 / Bill C-75
leads.documents: Repealed archaic anal intercourse offence that continued to affect young men; set age of consent at 16 for all activities; enforcement history relevant to police interaction risk.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Bill C-32 introduced Nov 15, 2016, incorporated into Bill C-75 tabled late March 2018, royal assent June 21, 2019; statement by MP Randy Boissonnault special advisor on LGBTQ2 issues.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act
leads.documents: Federal law allowing RCMP and federal departments to destroy/remove judicial records for historic homosexual acts and former s.159 anal intercourse convictions; distinguishes expungement from pardon/record suspension.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: French title 'Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques'; Governor General granted royal assent June 21, 2018; Parole Board of Canada explanation cited.

leads.title: Manitoba same-sex adoption legalization (2002)
leads.documents: Documents parental/family rights machinery in Manitoba specifically; Manitoba listed as legalizing same-sex adoption in 2002 alongside Quebec, Newfoundland and Labrador, Northwest Territories.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'Manitoba (2002)' in adoption paragraph; first province British Columbia 1996, last Nunavut 2011.

leads.title: Provincial human rights laws including sexual orientation and gender identity (as of 2017) - includes Manitoba
leads.documents: Documents anti-discrimination and anti-harassment protections in employment, housing and public/private accommodations; provincial laws cover most schools, rental housing, health care and workplaces in Manitoba.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'As of 2017, all provinces, territories, and the federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity as prohibited grounds'; Canadian Human Rights Act limited to federal jurisdiction vs provincial jurisdiction explanation.

leads.title: Federal Court Challenges Program (expanded 1985) + Government apologies
leads.documents: Documents rights-enforcement machinery and official acknowledgment of enforcement history: funding for Charter equality test cases; PM Justin Trudeau apology Nov 28, 2017 and Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police apology Dec 2020 for decades of oppression, institutional bias and Charter violations.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: Program expanded 1985 to fund test cases; Trudeau apology quote dated Nov 28, 2017 in Parliament; CACP apology dated December 2020 on International Day of Human Rights with Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee mandate.
